biography.plain_text: Sergey Gvardeitsev founded Itransition, a software development business that grew out of his work at Belarusian technology group Belhard. Trained in applied mathematics at Belarusian State University, he credited Belhard's Igor Mamonenko as a business mentor. He later handed the company's daily management to Alex Demichev in 2016 while remaining chairman.

long_biography.plain_text:
Software entrepreneur Sergey Gvardeitsev used teaching to find future colleagues. His university elective attracted talented programmers, including competition winners, and he tested them with timed team exercises. One student's ability to solve difficult problems intuitively particularly impressed him. The recruits became the nucleus of a development team, and a company training centre later supplied further new employees.

To reach American customers directly, he sent experienced Minsk staff to establish an Austin office. Removing intermediaries brought the developers closer to clients and improved margins. The American operation also offered consulting and complete solutions, extending the business beyond selling programmers' time by the hour.
